title: Think Past the First Consequence
coreMove: Follow a decision through reactions, delays, and displaced costs before accepting the first visible win.
sourcePressure: The source says actions sit inside systems with intended and unintended consequences. Higher-order effects, reactions from other people, paying too much, pushing too fast, delayed effects, and many-path failure can make the first visible result misleading.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is vague long-term thinking. The chapter must show a visible chain: first effect, second response, delayed cost, displaced burden, then a better move.

hook: The first win can hide the real loss
counterintuition: Short term versus long term generic contrast

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: city scooter parking policy near a commuter rail station
exampleSpecs.audience: Olivia, a transportation planner under pressure to clear sidewalks before Monday
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a quick ban moves the problem into wheelchair ramps and train exits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia walks the ban route at 7:40 a.m., marks where riders will drop scooters next, and changes the policy to add corrals before enforcement starts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a row of scooters leaning against a rain-dark rail-station wall

exampleSpecs.domain: fisheries co-op negotiating a higher catch quota after a good season
exampleSpecs.audience: Nicolas, a co-op analyst whose members want the immediate revenue bump
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether first-year income damages next year's stock and the buyer relationship
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nicolas asks the room to predict buyer response and stock response separately, then places both consequences on the same harbor map
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What happens after the first full hold leaves the dock?

exampleSpecs.domain: SaaS sales team offering an aggressive annual discount to close quarter
exampleSpecs.audience: Chiara, a revenue operations lead watching the deal desk celebrate
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a first-quarter win resets renewal expectations and traps support capacity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chiara adds renewal price, support hours, and competitor expectations under the discount line before approving the contract
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 5:18 p.m., Chiara sees the discount field flash red in the deal desk
mustAvoid: generic sales bonus incentive scene from chapter 2

exampleSpecs.domain: middle school cafeteria replacing hot lunch with faster grab-and-go meals
exampleSpecs.audience: Yusuf, a district nutrition coordinator trying to reduce lunch lines
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether shorter lines produce more wasted food and hungry students by last period
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Yusuf weighs the untouched packaged meals after dismissal and traces the first consequence of speed into the delayed consequence of afternoon nurse visits
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cold plastic clamshells stacked beside a humming cafeteria scale

exampleSpecs.domain: warehouse automation rollout that speeds picking but jams packing
exampleSpecs.audience: Daniel, an operations manager offered a vendor pilot before holiday peak
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether improving one station shifts congestion and overtime into another
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel follows one order ticket from robot pick to packing table and records where the saved minutes reappear as a queue
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bent order ticket taped to the side of a stalled packing chute

exampleSpecs.domain: airline boarding experiment that boards window seats first
exampleSpecs.audience: Ingrid, a gate supervisor testing a faster boarding script on a snowy evening
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a faster first scan creates overhead-bin fights and missed connections later
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ingrid stops timing at door closure rather than last scanned pass, then rewrites the metric after seeing the bin conflict delay
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "We shaved six minutes," the gate agent says while a stroller blocks the jet bridge

skillTargets: trace a decision beyond the first visible result
choose action without becoming paralyzed by complexity

tryThisNowSpec: For one planned move, write the first result, the likely reaction from someone else, and the quiet cost that appears one week later.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
